prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Regional Dispatch Center (operational name Juniper) intakes calls, records incidents, coordinates triage/dispatch, jurisdictions and shared awareness. Jurisdictions retain resource ownership/local policy and maintain/review response zones/routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center as clinical direction, access, roads, weather, closures and capacity require. Ambulance Coordination Platform shares coverage/incidents/availability, consolidates unit position/status for regional comparison. Computer Aided Dispatch Console supports entry, assessment and maps; displays incident/priority, travel, availability/access, and staging options accounting for demand, travel and access; staff verify currency. Regional Dispatch Center maintains regional coverage picture from unit locations, crew reports/readiness. North Gate Status Board produces North Approach [status]; North and South Gate Status Boards support routing when access changes; South Gate Status Board displays southern entry conditions. Call Taker Mara (radio alias Larkspur) validates location before medical details; captures location/callback/patient/condition/barriers, distinguishes observed/secondhand reports, resolves uncertainty, remains engaged as needed, updates before dispatch. Center preserves original report with clarifications; Mara produces Caller Location Correction Slip. Triage Supervisor (operational name Copperfield) assigns/confirms priority by life threat, time sensitivity, deterioration; urgent threats prompt dispatch; reviews conflicts/uncertainty/worsening/escalation, records rationale, confirms response matches caller information, sends Pediatric Acuity Note; consults Regional Medical Director when time permits without delaying urgent response. Medical Director sets protocols/advises unusual needs, not dispatch authority. Data Quality Officer (operational name Pebble) flags defects/reviews recording, does not change priority. Selection follows priority/requirements; weighs clinical need, travel, capability, readiness, coverage. Dispatchers recommend; authorize per regional rules, record unit, conditions, authorization time/reason. Radio Coordinator (call sign Mistral) monitors Regional Radio Network, verifies channels/backup/reachability, selects available talkgroup; transmits incident ID, location, priority, assignment, hazards; confirms approved route changes before diversion. Paramedic Crew acknowledges/repeats location and priority; reports material changes/conflicts and statuses (available/responding/on scene/transporting/unavailable) promptly. Correct discrepancies by fresh transmission; absent prompt acknowledgment, retry and alert dispatch supervisor. Handoff requires crew acknowledgment and dispatch confirmation of essentials. Crew reports position/status entering/leaving staging; stays at assigned point until dispatch confirms relocation/direct response. Ambulance Unit 417 follows instructions, requests unsafe-detail clarification.

New part:
S137: Shift Commander sends the Mutual Aid Release Form when a neighboring service is released from regional coverage.
S138: Regional Dispatch Center uses the swap voucher to confirm that a unit's battery readiness is current before it is placed in service.
S139: Regional Dispatch Center uses the queue snapshot to account for congestion approaching the northern entry before assigning a route.
S140: North Gate Status Board displays the latest queue condition and access restriction for units approaching the northern entry.
S141: Triage Supervisor advises dispatch when changes in clinical demand may require repositioning available units.
S142: Regional Medical Director establishes clinical priorities that dispatch applies when assigning units during elevated demand.
S143: Hospital Liaison Desk provides receiving-facility capacity information for consideration during transport planning.
S144: Dispatchers compare projected response times with remaining coverage before moving a unit away from its current area.
S145: Data Quality Officer reviews inconsistent location or status reports and routes corrections through the established operational process.
S146: Ambulance Coordination Platform retains time-stamped status changes so supervisors can review the sequence of unit movement.
S147: A crew advises dispatch when a road closure, unsafe condition, or unexpected delay makes the assigned route unsuitable.
S148: Regional Dispatch Center records the approved alternative route and checks that the change does not leave a critical area without reasonable coverage.
S149: The Hospital Liaison Desk coordinates destination consultation when a patient’s condition or the operating status of a facility may affect the assignment.
S150: The consultation uses the patient’s reported condition, transport estimate, and current facility acceptance information available to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S151: The Regional Medical Director provides clinical guidance when destination selection involves a specialized capability or a regional care protocol.
S152: The Hospital Liaison Desk contacts the Emergency Department to confirm whether the proposed destination can receive the patient.
S153: The Regional Dispatch Center uses the correction slip to reconcile a reported destination change with the active incident record.
S154: Larkspur confirms the incident identifier and intended receiving facility before the destination request is transmitted.
S155: The Emergency Department advises the Hospital Liaison Desk of relevant capacity limits, access constraints, or changes to its receiving status.
S156: The Hospital Liaison Desk records the consultation outcome and communicates any destination restriction to the Regional Dispatch Center.
S157: The Regional Dispatch Center evaluates the consultation outcome against patient acuity, transport time, and available ambulance coverage.
S158: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents the approved destination and any associated operational instructions to dispatch staff.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
